title: Lie spaces of scheme centralizers and normalizers as group invariants
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and all subgroups are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. For such a group $J$, put $\operatorname{Lie}(J)=T_{J/F,e}$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], equivalently the tangent vectors $\ker(J(F[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2)\to J(F))$. These are finite-dimensional $F$-vector spaces, and closed subgroup inclusions induce injective tangent maps. Conjugation by $G$ induces a rational linear action $\operatorname{Ad}$ on $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. For every closed subgroup $H\subseteq G$, $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}(H)$ is $H$-stable for this action, so $H$ acts on $\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h$. For a rational action of a group $J$ on a vector space $V$, write $V^J=\{v:\operatorname{Ad}(j)(v\otimes1)=v\otimes1\text{ for all commutative }F\text{-algebras }A\text{ and }j\in J(A)\}$, using the given action in place of $\operatorname{Ad}$ for general $V$.

Let $K,H\subseteq G$, with $H$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose $C,N\subseteq G$ are closed subgroup schemes representing the functors
$$C(A)=\{g\in G(A):g_{A'}k=kg_{A'}\text{ for all commutative }A\text{-algebras }A'\text{ and }k\in K(A')\},$$
$$N(A)=\{g\in G(A):g_{A'}H(A')g_{A'}^{-1}=H(A')\text{ for all commutative }A\text{-algebras }A'\}.$$
Then, as subspaces of $\mathfrak g$ and $\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h$, respectively,
$$\operatorname{Lie}(C)=\mathfrak g^K,\qquad \operatorname{Lie}(N)/\mathfrak h=(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h)^H.$$
No characteristic-zero, connectedness, reductivity, or smoothness of $C$ or $N$ is assumed. These are invariants of the whole group functor, not invariants of its Lie algebra.

source.place: Proposition 10.34 and proof, printed pp.197–198; tangent functor and adjoint action in Sections 10a–10d, printed pp.184–193. The smooth-H specialization suffices here; representability is an explicit hypothesis, not asserted in this node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus] to the groups and inclusions in the statement. This gives finite-dimensional tangent spaces, injective linear tangent maps, the rational action $\operatorname{Ad}_G$, and its compatibility with subgroup inclusions. For $h\in H(R)$ and $u\in\mathfrak h\otimes_F R$, that compatibility says $\operatorname{Ad}_G(h)u$ is the image of $\operatorname{Ad}_H(h)u$. Thus $\mathfrak h$ is $H$-stable. The induced quotient action is rational: in a basis of $\mathfrak g$ extending a basis of $\mathfrak h$, its matrix is the quotient diagonal block of the regular matrix of the restricted action; the inverse comes from $h^{-1}$. Write $E_R$ for $E_{G,R}$, with formal parameter $\delta$. Choose such a vector-space basis once. It also shows for every $R$ that the kernel of $\mathfrak g\otimes_F R\to(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h)\otimes_F R$ is exactly $\mathfrak h\otimes_F R$; this uses only the direct-sum decomposition given by the basis.

source.place: Proposition 10.34, printed pp.197–198; dual-number calculus 10.6, 10.11, 10.14, 10.19–10.21, printed pp.188–193. The normalizer calculation omitted in the source is supplied explicitly.

proof.text: Let $D=F[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ and $v\in\mathfrak g$. If $v\in\operatorname{Lie}(C)$, its tangent point $E_F(v)$ lies in $C(D)$. For any commutative $F$-algebra $R$ and $k\in K(R)$, use the $D$-algebra $R[\delta]$ with $\epsilon\mapsto\delta$. The defining centralizer property gives $kE_R(v\otimes1)k^{-1}=E_R(v\otimes1)$. The conjugation identity and injectivity of $E_R$ in [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus] give $\operatorname{Ad}(k)(v\otimes1)=v\otimes1$. This is exactly $v\in\mathfrak g^K$. Conversely suppose $v\in\mathfrak g^K$. For any $D$-algebra $S$ and $k\in K(S)$, apply that invariance with $R=S$ to obtain $kE_S(v\otimes1)k^{-1}=E_S(v\otimes1)$ in $G(S[\delta])$. Apply the ring map $S[\delta]\to S$ that fixes $S$ and sends $\delta\mapsto\epsilon_S$, the image of $\epsilon$ in $S$; it is defined since $\epsilon_S^2=0$. Naturality of $E$ identifies the specialized point with the image of $E_F(v)$. It commutes with every such $k$, so $E_F(v)\in C(D)$ and $v\in\operatorname{Lie}(C)$.

source.place: Proposition 10.34, printed pp.197–198; dual-number calculus 10.6, 10.11, 10.14, 10.19–10.21, printed pp.188–193. The normalizer calculation omitted in the source is supplied explicitly.

proof.text:
Every element of $H(A)$ conjugates $H(A')$ onto itself after every extension $A\to A'$, so $H\subseteq N$ as subgroup functors and $\mathfrak h\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(N)$. For $v\in\operatorname{Lie}(N)$, $E_F(v)\in N(D)$. Fix a commutative $F$-algebra $R$ and $h\in H(R)$, and apply the normalizer property over the $D$-algebra $R[\delta]$, $\epsilon\mapsto\delta$. Then $E_R(v_R)hE_R(-v_R)h^{-1}$ lies in $H(R[\delta])$ and reduces to the identity, where $v_R=v\otimes1$. By addition and conjugation in [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus] it equals
$$E_R(v_R-\operatorname{Ad}(h)v_R).$$
The subgroup-kernel identification in that node therefore gives $v_R-\operatorname{Ad}(h)v_R\in\mathfrak h\otimes_F R$. The quotient-kernel description in step 1 says exactly that the class of $v$ is fixed by every $h\in H(R)$, for every $R$. Hence $\operatorname{Lie}(N)/\mathfrak h\subseteq(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h)^H$.

source.place: Proposition 10.34, printed pp.197–198; dual-number calculus 10.6, 10.11, 10.14, 10.19–10.21, printed pp.188–193. The normalizer calculation omitted in the source is supplied explicitly.

proof.text:
Conversely let $v\in\mathfrak g$ have $H$-fixed class. For every commutative $F$-algebra $R$ and $h\in H(R)$, step 1 gives $v_R-\operatorname{Ad}(h)v_R\in\mathfrak h\otimes_F R$. The addition, conjugation and subgroup-kernel formulas of [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus] give
$$E_R(v_R)hE_R(-v_R)h^{-1}=E_R(v_R-\operatorname{Ad}(h)v_R)\in H(R[\delta]).$$
Take any $D$-algebra $S$ and $h\in H(S)$, set $R=S$ in this formula, and apply $S[\delta]\to S$, $\delta\mapsto\epsilon_S$. If $x$ is the image of $E_F(v)$ in $G(S)$, naturality gives $xhx^{-1}h^{-1}\in H(S)$, hence $xhx^{-1}\in H(S)$. Apply the same calculation to $-v$ (its quotient class is also fixed) to obtain $x^{-1}H(S)x\subseteq H(S)$. The two inclusions imply $xH(S)x^{-1}=H(S)$. This holds for every $D$-algebra $S$, so the defining functor of $N$ gives $E_F(v)\in N(D)$, whence $v\in\operatorname{Lie}(N)$.

source.place: Proposition 10.34, printed pp.197–198; dual-number calculus 10.6, 10.11, 10.14, 10.19–10.21, printed pp.188–193. The normalizer calculation omitted in the source is supplied explicitly.

proof.text: The preceding two steps identify $\operatorname{Lie}(N)$ with the inverse image of $(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h)^H$ under the quotient map $q:\mathfrak g\to\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h$. Since $q$ is surjective and its kernel is $\mathfrak h\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(N)$, restriction of $q$ induces an injective map $\operatorname{Lie}(N)/\mathfrak h\to\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h$ whose image is exactly that fixed subspace: lift any fixed class to a vector $v$ and apply step 4. This proves the second equality as subspaces. Step 2 proves the first equality. All tests used arbitrary commutative algebras and the specified subgroup functors; no assertion about Lie-algebra invariants, or about smoothness of $C$ or $N$, entered.
